components.note: 氵 (water) — mud is earth soaked with water
尼 (ní) gives the sound — it matches 泥's reading exactly

example.hanzi: 孩子们在泥里玩得很开心。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài ní lǐ wán de hěn kāixīn.
example.english: The kids are having a great time playing in the mud.
example.fact: 泥 is the everyday word for mud and clay, and it appears in 水泥 (cement, literally "water mud"), 泥土 and 泥巴. A rarer reading nì means "to plaster," but ní is the one you will meet constantly.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — the original sense was patching garments
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound — it matches 补's reading exactly

example.hanzi: 这件衣服破了，需要补一补。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu pò le, xūyào bǔ yi bǔ.
example.english: This garment is torn and needs mending.
example.fact: From patching clothes, 补 grew into "making up for a shortfall": 补课 (a make-up class), 补充 (to add), 补习 (cram school). It also covers nourishing the body, as in 补品 (tonic foods), a big theme in Chinese winter eating habits.

components.note: 土 (earth) — walls and blockages were once built of earth
者 (zhě) is the listed sound part, though today the match to dǔ is only loose

example.hanzi: 路上堵车了，我会晚一点到。
example.pinyin: Lù shàng dǔ chē le, wǒ huì wǎn yìdiǎn dào.
example.english: There is a traffic jam, so I will arrive a bit late.
example.fact: 堵车 (traffic jam) is one of the most common complaints in Chinese city life. 堵 also describes a blocked nose (鼻子堵了) or feeling choked up (心里堵得慌), and it doubles as the measure word for walls: 一堵墙.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — a fish hook is a metal tool
勺 (sháo) is the sound/shape hint — the hooked shape suggests a bent hook

example.hanzi: 爸爸周末喜欢去河边钓鱼。
example.pinyin: Bàba zhōumò xǐhuan qù hébiān diào yú.
example.english: Dad likes to go fishing by the river on weekends.
example.fact: 钓鱼 means fishing with a rod, as opposed to 捕鱼 (catching fish with nets). The same word is used for online phishing, 网络钓鱼, and the name of the disputed Diaoyu Islands (钓鱼岛) uses it too.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant a flower or blossom
央 (yāng) gives the sound — it is close to yīng

example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīngxióng jiù le hěn duō rén.
example.english: This hero saved many people.
example.fact: 英 began as a flower, then came to mean the "flower" of people: the outstanding ones, as in 英雄, 英俊 (handsome) and 精英 (elite). It is also the short form for Britain and English: 英国, 英语.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the character is built around a bow shape
丨 (vertical strokes) — two upright strokes cross the bow, which the dictionary reads as something being bound or straightened

example.pinyin: Liǎng zhě xiāngbǐ, wǒ fú rú tā.
example.english: Comparing the two, I am not as good as he is.
example.fact: 弗 is a classical negative meaning "not," now surviving in set phrases like 弗如 and 自愧弗如 (to feel inferior to). In modern writing it appears mostly in transliterated names such as 弗洛伊德 (Freud) and 弗吉尼亚 (Virginia).

excludeSuggestion: Literary negative that is rare on its own; mostly met in set phrases and transliterated foreign names.

components.note: 氏 (shì) sits at the top; traditionally read as the sun sinking low
日 (sun) — the sun going down gives the original meaning, dusk

example.pinyin: Tā tóu yūn de hūn guòqu le.
example.english: He was so dizzy that he fainted.
example.fact: 昏 originally meant dusk (黄昏), when light fades, and then extended to dim senses: 昏迷 (coma), 昏倒 (to faint), and 头昏 (lightheaded). Confusion also fits, as in 昏头昏脑 (muddle-headed).

components.note: 方 forms the left side; here it is part of the character's structure rather than meaning "square" or "direction"
㐌 on the right is a variant of 也, the same piece seen in 驰 and 弛

example.hanzi: 政府正在施行新的规定。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài shīxíng xīn de guīdìng.
example.english: The government is putting new regulations into effect.
example.fact: 施 lives mostly inside compounds: 实施 (to implement), 施工 (under construction, seen on signs), 施肥 (to fertilize), 施加压力 (to apply pressure). It is also a surname, as in 西施, one of China's legendary beauties.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — picking is done by hand
啇 on the right stands for the fruit hanging from a branch, per the dictionary's reading

example.hanzi: 小朋友们在果园里摘苹果。
example.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyoumen zài guǒyuán lǐ zhāi píngguǒ.
example.english: The children are picking apples in the orchard.
example.fact: 摘 is used for picking fruit and flowers off a plant, and also for taking something off: 摘眼镜 (take off glasses), 摘帽子. Leaves and tea are usually 采 (cǎi) instead, and 摘要 means an abstract or summary.

components.note: 口 on top works like a loop or hanging point in the shape
巾 (cloth) hangs below, which fits the idea of something dangling

example.pinyin: Bǎ dēng diào zài tiānhuābǎn shàng ba.
example.english: Let's hang the lamp from the ceiling.
example.fact: 吊 gives many everyday words: 吊灯 (chandelier), 吊桥 (suspension bridge), 吊车 (crane), 吊带 (straps). In mainland slang, 吊 can also mean "awesome," as in 吊炸天. 吊唁 means to pay condolences.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early writing was done on bamboo strips
间 (jiān) gives the sound — it is close to jiǎn

example.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ hěn jiǎndān.
example.english: This method is very simple.
example.fact: Before paper, Chinese was written on bamboo slips (竹简); short, narrow slips led to the sense of "brief" and "simple." You see it in 简单, 简历 (résumé), 简称 (abbreviation) and 简体字 (simplified characters).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breathing out and scolding both involve the mouth
可 (kě) gives a rough sound hint for hē

example.hanzi: 他呵了一口气，暖了暖手。
example.pinyin: Tā hē le yì kǒu qì, nuǎnle nuǎn shǒu.
example.english: He breathed on his hands to warm them.
example.fact: 呵 literally means to puff out warm breath (呵气) and to scold (呵斥). It also gives 呵护 (to cherish and protect) and the laugh 呵呵, which in chats can sound curt or even sarcastic. A neutral particle reading ā/a also exists.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — lips frame the mouth
辰 (chén) gives the sound — close to chún

example.hanzi: 她的嘴唇很干，要涂润唇膏。
example.pinyin: Tā de zuǐchún hěn gān, yào tú rùnchúngāo.
example.english: Her lips are dry, so she needs lip balm.
example.fact: On its own 唇 is mostly bound; people say 嘴唇 for lip. Related words are 唇膏 (lipstick) and the idiom 唇亡齿寒, "if the lips are gone, the teeth get cold," about neighbours whose fates are linked.

components.note: 阝 (mound) — a raised hill fits the idea of something rising
生 (grow) — plausibly the idea of swelling growth

example.pinyin: Jīntiān de huìyì hěn lóngzhòng.
example.english: Today's meeting is very grand.
example.fact: 隆 means high, grand or flourishing: 隆重 (solemn and grand), 隆冬 (the depths of winter), 隆起 (to bulge). It also appears in 乾隆, the Qianlong emperor's era name, and in 轰隆, a rumbling sound.

components.note: A picture of the wooden frame placed around the mouth of a well, seen from above

example.pinyin: Cūnzi lǐ yǒu yì kǒu lǎo jǐng.
example.english: There is an old well in the village.
example.fact: The measure word for wells is 口: 一口井. 井 also appears in 水井 (water well), 油井 (oil well), 天井 (courtyard), and the idiom 井井有条 (in perfect order). Because of its shape, 井 is the Chinese name for the # symbol.

components.note: 死 (death) — the character is about dying
比 (bǐ) gives the sound — it is close to bì

example.hanzi: 警察当场把那个坏人击毙了。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá dāngchǎng bǎ nàge huàirén jībì le.
example.english: The police shot the criminal dead on the spot.
example.fact: 毙 appears in 击毙 and 枪毙 (to shoot dead). In office talk it has a colloquial sense, "to reject": 方案被毙了 means "the proposal got shot down," borrowing the violent image.

components.note: 攵 (tap, action) — the character is connected with an action of sending
至 (zhì) gives the sound — it matches exactly and also means "to arrive"

example.hanzi: 大雨导致了严重的堵车。
example.pinyin: Dàyǔ dǎozhì le yánzhòng de dǔchē.
example.english: The heavy rain caused a serious traffic jam.
example.fact: 导致 usually introduces a bad outcome, unlike neutral 引起 or positive 促成. 致 itself conveys messages: 致谢, 致电, 致辞 (give a speech), and letters close with 此致敬礼. Also 致富 (to get rich) and 一致 (in agreement).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — holding something in custody is a hand action
甲 (jiǎ) gives only a loose sound hint, sharing the -a vowel

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ xiǎotōu yā zǒu le.
example.english: The police took the thief away in custody.
example.fact: 押 covers both holding people (押送, to escort) and putting up security. 押金 is the deposit you pay when renting an apartment or bike; rentals are often described as 押一付三. 押韵 (yā yùn) means to rhyme.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the original name came from the Han River
又 replaces the complicated right half of traditional 漢 in the simplified form

example.pinyin: Tā shì Hànzú rén, huì shuō Hànyǔ.
example.english: He is Han Chinese and speaks Chinese.
example.fact: 汉 comes from the Han dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), which gave the Chinese majority its name: 汉族, 汉语 (Chinese language), 汉字 (characters). It also means a man in 好汉 (a brave fellow) and 男子汉 (a real man).

components.note: 大 (big) forms the upper part
示 (altar, to show) forms the lower part; the combination is read as a person facing spirits

example.pinyin: Tā wúnài de xiào le xiào.
example.english: He smiled helplessly.
example.fact: 奈 is almost never used alone. Key forms are 无奈 (helpless) and 无可奈何 (nothing to be done), plus 奈何 ("what can be done"). In foreign names it gives the sound, as in 奈良 (Nara) and 奈飞 (Netflix).

components.note: 立 (stand) — the upper part
里 (inside) — the lower part; the dictionary reads a child standing in a village

example.hanzi: 这个儿童乐园很受欢迎。
example.pinyin: Zhège értóng lèyuán hěn shòu huānyíng.
example.english: This children's playground is very popular.
example.fact: 童 is mostly bound: 儿童 (children), 童年 (childhood), 童话 (fairy tale), 童装 (children's clothes). In classical Chinese 童 could also mean a young servant boy before it settled on "child."

components.note: 亻 (person) — leaning or being partial describes people
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound — close to piān

example.hanzi: 我越不想去，他偏偏要我去。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yuè bù xiǎng qù, tā piānpiān yào wǒ qù.
example.english: The less I wanted to go, the more he insisted that I go.
example.fact: 偏 means leaning to one side, so 偏心 is favoritism and 偏见 is prejudice. The adverb 偏偏 expresses "of all things" or "stubbornly," often with annoyance. 偏旁 is also the term for a character's component.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偶 first meant a human-like figurine
禺 (yù) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā ǒu'ěr huì lái wǒ jiā chī fàn.
example.english: He occasionally comes to my house for dinner.
example.fact: 偶尔 means "once in a while" while 偶然 means "by chance." 偶 also means pairs: 偶数 (even numbers), 配偶 (spouse). And 偶像 (idol) and 木偶 (puppet) come from its older "figurine" sense.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a family relation
白 (bái) gives the sound — a rough match for bó

example.pinyin: Wǒ bóbo shì yīshēng.
example.english: My uncle is a doctor.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms are precise: 伯伯 is your father's elder brother, 叔叔 his younger brother. 伯伯 can also be a polite address to an older man outside the family. 伯 is also the "earl" rank in the old five noble titles.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — dogs were once used as ritual offerings
南 (nán) is listed as the sound part, but the match to xiàn is weak today

example.hanzi: 他把一生献给了教育事业。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yìshēng xiàn gěi le jiàoyù shìyè.
example.english: He dedicated his whole life to education.
example.fact: 献 is a formal way to give: 献花 (present flowers), 献血 (donate blood), 献礼 (offer a tribute), 贡献 (contribution). Compared with the everyday 送, 献 implies respect, devotion, or a solemn occasion.

components.note: 口 and 十 are pieces of an older character 叶 (xié, "to harmonize"), reused in simplification
十 (ten) — together with 口 it does not describe a leaf; the meaning comes from borrowing

example.pinyin: Qiūtiān dào le, shùyè dōu huáng le.
example.english: Autumn has come and the leaves have all turned yellow.
example.fact: 叶 is the simplified form of 葉. The simplification borrowed an existing old character 叶 (xié, "harmonize"), so one glyph now serves for "leaf." It is also a surname in the form 叶, and the word is 叶子 or 树叶.

components.note: 八 (divide) — the upper part means to split apart
厶 (private) — dividing what is private gives "public"

example.hanzi: 我每天坐公共汽车去上班。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zuò gōnggòng qìchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: I take the bus to work every day.
example.fact: 公 has two big branches: "public/fair" (公平, 公园, 公司) and "male" for animals (公鸡 rooster, 公牛 bull), opposed to 母. In measures, 公 is the metric prefix: 公里 (kilometre), 公斤 (kilogram).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the action uses the teeth and mouth
盍 (hé) gives the sound — a near match for kè

example.hanzi: 他喜欢一边看电视一边嗑瓜子。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yìbiān kàn diànshì yìbiān kè guāzǐ.
example.english: He likes to crack sunflower seeds while watching TV.
example.fact: 嗑瓜子 is a classic snack habit in China, especially at Spring Festival. Online, 嗑 has gained a slang sense: 嗑CP means to enjoy a fictional or celebrity couple, savoring the pairing like a snack.

components.note: 亻 (person) — leaning on someone else is a human relation
衣 (yī) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yī fǎ bàn shì.
example.english: We must handle matters in accordance with the law.
example.fact: 依 is the more formal, written cousin of 按 (according to): 依法 (in accordance with the law), 依据 (basis). As "to rely on," it appears in 依靠, 依赖 and 依依不舍 (reluctant to part); 依然 means "still."

components.note: 忄 (heart) — sympathy is a feeling
血 (xuè) gives the sound — a close match for xù

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī hěn tǐxù xuésheng.
example.english: The teacher is very considerate toward her students.
example.fact: 恤 means to feel for and help others: 体恤 (to empathize) and 抚恤金 (a pension for bereaved families). Most people see it in T恤, the standard Chinese for T-shirt, where it was chosen purely for its sound.

components.note: 马 (horse) — the original meaning was to harness horses to a carriage
加 (jiā) gives the sound — close to jià

example.hanzi: 他刚拿到驾照，开车很小心。
example.pinyin: Tā gāng ná dào jiàzhào, kāichē hěn xiǎoxīn.
example.english: He just got his driver's license and drives very carefully.
example.fact: 驾 was about harnessing horses to a cart, and today covers all kinds of driving: 驾驶, 驾照. It also gives honorific words: 劳驾 (excuse me, may I trouble you) and 大驾光临 (your esteemed presence).

components.note: 纟 (silk) — the original sense was pure, undyed silk
屯 (tún) gives the sound — a near match for chún

example.hanzi: 这杯果汁是纯的，没加糖。
example.pinyin: Zhè bēi guǒzhī shì chún de, méi jiā táng.
example.english: This juice is pure, with no added sugar.
example.fact: 纯 describes something unmixed: 纯棉 (pure cotton, seen on clothing labels), 纯净水 (purified water), 单纯 (simple, naive), 纯洁 (pure). 纯属 means "purely" and is used to deny things: 纯属误会 (a pure misunderstanding).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the action is done with the hands
皮 (pí) gives the sound — close to pī

example.hanzi: 她在肩上披了一件外套。
example.pinyin: Tā zài jiān shàng pī le yí jiàn wàitào.
example.english: She draped a coat over her shoulders.
example.fact: 披 means to throw something loosely over your shoulders without putting arms in the sleeves: 披肩 (shawl), 披头散发 (hair hanging loose). It also means to reveal, as in 披露, and is the first syllable of 披萨 (pizza).

components.note: 氵 (water) — dregs are what settles in liquid
查 (chá) gives the sound — a close match for zhā

example.pinyin: Kāfēi zhā kěyǐ yòng lái zhòng huā.
example.english: Coffee grounds can be used for growing flowers.
example.fact: 渣 means leftover bits: 豆渣 (soy pulp), 煤渣 (cinders), 饼干渣 (biscuit crumbs). Online, 渣男 ("scum guy") and 渣女 are common slang terms for unfaithful or heartless partners.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — hats were made from cloth
冒 (mào) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Tiānqì lěng, nǐ dàishang màozi ba.
example.english: It is cold, so put on a hat.
example.fact: 帽 is normally paired as 帽子, with the measure word 顶: 一顶帽子. You 戴 (wear) a hat. Figuratively, 扣帽子 means to slap a label on someone, and 高帽子 means flattery.

components.note: 龺 on the left is a reduced form of the older 倝 part
韦 (wéi) is the simplified form of 韋, "tanned leather"

example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù Hánguó lǚyóu.
example.english: She wants to travel to South Korea.
example.fact: In modern usage 韩 stands for Korea (韩国 South Korea, 韩语 Korean, 韩剧 K-drama). It is the same character as the ancient Chinese state of Han and the surname, but the Korean name 한 simply happens to be written with it.

components.note: 丰 (abundant) — richness of color
色 (colour) — what makes something look vivid

example.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ de huā kāi de hěn yàn.
example.english: The flowers in the yard are blooming brilliantly.
example.fact: 艳 describes vivid, rich colour: 鲜艳 (brightly coloured), 艳丽 (gorgeous), 艳阳天 (a bright, sunny day). 艳遇 means a romantic encounter, and 艳 is often attached to flowers or dresses.

components.note: A heavily simplified form of 業 whose strokes no longer show a clear picture

example.hanzi: 他毕业以后在上海工作。
example.pinyin: Tā bìyè yǐhòu zài Shànghǎi gōngzuò.
example.english: After graduating he worked in Shanghai.
example.fact: 业 rarely stands alone; it builds 毕业 (to graduate), 职业 (occupation), 企业 (enterprise), 业余 (spare-time, amateur), and 作业 (homework). In Buddhism, 业 also translates karma.

components.note: 𠂇 is an old left-hand shape
又 (hand) — two hands joined suggest friendship and also hint the sound

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: He is my best friend.
example.fact: 友 is bound: 朋友 (friend), 友好 (friendly), 友谊 (friendship), 校友 (alumnus), 室友 (roommate), and 网友 (online friend). The old picture is two hands clasped, an apt image for friendship.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — the old meaning was the appearance of a dog
丬 is a simplified stand-in for the left half, only a rough sound clue

example.pinyin: Tā xiànzài de zhuàngtài hěn hǎo.
example.english: He is in great form right now.
example.fact: 状 covers appearance and condition (状态, 现状, 症状 symptoms) but also a document: 奖状 (certificate of merit), 告状 (to tattle or file a complaint). 状元 was the top scorer in the old imperial exams.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — three mouths together suggest many, as in a variety of goods or many voices judging

example.hanzi: 这家店卖很多进口食品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài hěn duō jìnkǒu shípǐn.
example.english: This store sells many imported food products.
example.fact: 品 appears in 商品, 产品, 食品 (food products), and 作品 (a work of art). As a verb it means to savor: 品茶, 品尝. 品 once also meant official rank, as in 九品 (nine grades).

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — scars come from wounds or illness
艮 (gèn) gives the sound — it shares the -en final

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng liú xià le yìxiē hénjì.
example.english: Some marks were left on the wall.
example.fact: 痕 is mostly seen in compounds: 痕迹 (trace), 伤痕 (scar), 泪痕 (tear streaks), 裂痕 (crack). 裂痕 is also used figuratively for a rift in a relationship.

components.note: 田 (field) — here it is a picture of the fruit, not a field
木 (tree) — the fruit grows on a tree

example.hanzi: 我最喜欢吃的水果是苹果。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī de shuǐguǒ shì píngguǒ.
example.english: My favourite fruit is the apple.
example.fact: 果 is a fruit on a tree, and fruit became the metaphor for results: 结果 (result), 效果 (effect), 因果 (cause and effect), 果然 (as expected). In fruit names it often follows the type: 苹果, 水果.

components.note: 林 (lín) gives the sound — close to jìn
示 (altar) — taboos and sacred rules lie behind prohibition

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ jìnzhǐ xīyān.
example.english: Smoking is prohibited here.
example.fact: 禁止 is the standard word on "no" signs: 禁止吸烟 (no smoking). The same character has a second reading jīn meaning "to endure," in 禁不住 and 不禁. 紫禁城 (the Forbidden City) uses it too.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — flourishing greenery
木 (tree) — a tree in bloom
冖 (cover) — a roof-like shape from the old form

example.hanzi: 能在这里工作，我感到很荣幸。
example.pinyin: Néng zài zhèlǐ gōngzuò, wǒ gǎndào hěn róngxìng.
example.english: I feel very honored to work here.
example.fact: 荣 once meant a tree in bloom and developed into "glory": 荣幸 (honoured, a polite phrase), 光荣, 荣誉 (honour), 繁荣 (prosperous). It is also a surname.

components.note: 人 (person) — three people together stand for a crowd

example.pinyin: Guānzhòng dōu zhàn qǐlái gǔzhǎng.
example.english: The audience all stood up and applauded.
example.fact: 众 is three 人 stacked, a classic way to show "many." It builds 观众 (audience), 大众, 群众 (the masses), 公众 (the public), and the common phrase 众所周知 (as everyone knows).

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — the top part
日 sits below the fish; how it ties to "crude" is unclear

example.pinyin: Tā shuō huà yǒudiǎn lǔmǎng.
example.english: He speaks a bit rashly.
example.fact: 鲁 is the short name for Shandong province, after the ancient State of Lu, home of Confucius. The same character gives 鲁莽 (reckless), the surname Lu, and the writer 鲁迅 (Lu Xun).

components.note: 亻 (person) — originally a beautiful person
圭 (guī) is listed as the sound part, but the match to jiā is loose

example.hanzi: 我们需要找一个最佳方案。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào zhǎo yí ge zuìjiā fāng'àn.
example.english: We need to find the best solution.
example.fact: 佳 is a formal "good": 最佳 (best), 佳肴 (fine dishes), 佳节 (festive holiday). 每逢佳节倍思亲 is a famous line by Tang poet Wang Wei about missing family on holidays.

components.note: 比 (side by side) — two people together suggest "all"
白 sits below; its role is no longer clear

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì rénrén jiē zhī.
example.english: Everyone knows about this.
example.fact: 皆 is a formal, written equivalent of 都 (all). Like 都, it comes before the verb. It features in idioms 皆大欢喜 (everyone is happy) and 比比皆是 (found everywhere).

components.note: 糸 (silk or thread) at the bottom shows that the original meaning was rope
十 and 冖 above are read as a cord hanging from a cover, per the dictionary

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng sōusuǒ zīliào.
example.english: I search for information on the internet.
example.fact: 索 first meant a rope (绳索) and grew into "to look for" and "to demand": 搜索 (to search), 索引 (index), 索取 (to ask for), 线索 (clue, literally thread-rope). 索性 means "simply" or "might as well."
